eli5.text: When the assistant stops mid-response (like when you cancel it), the system now correctly saves your original message even if it never reached the server. ai.summary: cli/src/utils/strings.ts sets `LONG_TEXT_THRESHOLD` to 2000, doubling prior 1000 limit. Mechanism: pasted text exceeding threshold becomes attachment instead of inline insertion. Scope: CLI only. Detail: boundary check uses strictly greater than, so 2000 chars remain inline.

eli5.text: When you paste text into the command-line tool, it will stay in your message as long text only if it's shorter than 2,000 characters. ai.summary: Added `safeStringify` in `cli/src/utils/logger.ts` to handle circular references during log serialization. Replaces circular objects with `'[Circular]'` using a `WeakSet` tracker instead of throwing. Prevents crashes in dev mode when logging complex state objects.

eli5.text: When you're using the tool in development mode and it tries to log information about complex data, it used to crash if that data contained circular references (like an object that refers back to itself). Now it handles those gracefully by replacing the circular part with a placeholder text instead of crashing. If you looked, you'd see the word [Circular] appear in logs where the problematic data was, rather than the program stopping unexpectedly.

ai.title: CLI @ file search uses fuzzy matching with directory entries
ai.summary: CLI suggestion engine replaces exact path filtering with fuzzyMatch scoring gaps, consecutive runs, and word boundaries. common/src/project-file-tree.ts exports getAllPathsWithDirectories and PathInfo to include directory nodes in candidates. cli/src/hooks/use-suggestion-engine.ts consumes PathInfo[] and adds isDirectory plus matchScore to MatchedFileInfo. Score formula: gaps*10 - maxConsecutive*5 - boundaryBonus*15 + firstIndex, lower is better.

eli5.text: When you type an @ symbol and start searching for a file or folder in the command-line tool, matches are now found with looser, smarter logic: it no longer demands a perfect path match, and it can also surface folders (not just files) in the suggestions, scoring each result by how well its name lines up with what you typed (fewer gaps, longer consecutive runs, and word-start hits rank higher). You would notice this right away if you've ever tried to grab a file by a partial or misspelled name, since results now appear and improve even when the characters aren't typed in exact order. The improvement is live as of today.
